did_you_know.text: Did you know? Solomon begins his speech by saying that the LORD said he would dwell in a dark cloud, linking the LORD’s presence with a mysterious cloud or mist.
Did you know? Solomon says that the LORD did not initially choose a particular city or person to build the temple and lead the people; instead, he chose Jerusalem and David.
Did you know? Solomon presents the building of the temple as the fulfillment of the LORD’s word: David wanted to build the temple, but David’s son was the one who actually built it.
Did you know? Solomon made a large bronze basin in the temple, five cubits long and wide and three cubits high. He stood on it, knelt down, and spread out his hands toward heaven.
Did you know? Solomon emphasizes that even the highest heavens cannot contain the LORD. Therefore, the temple is not a place that confines him, but the place chosen for prayer and for turning to him.
Did you know? In his prayer, Solomon asks the LORD to judge fairly between people—to repay the wicked for his wrongdoing and to reward the righteous according to his righteousness.
Did you know? Solomon’s prayer also includes the foreigner—someone who is not an Israelite—if that person comes from a distant land and prays toward the temple for the sake of the LORD’s name.
Did you know? Solomon acknowledges that no one is without sin, and he describes the possibility of sin, exile, repentance, and prayer to the LORD.
Did you know? According to the prayer, true repentance is described as returning to the LORD with all one’s heart and soul, even when the Israelites are living in the land of their exile.

Did you know? At the end of the prayer, Solomon asks the LORD to arise and come to his resting place, together with the Ark of his strength; he asks that the priests be clothed with salvation and that the LORD’s faithful people rejoice in his goodness.
